question: A combination of vehicles falls into Class A when the gross combination weight rating (GCWR) is 26,001 pounds or more, provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is more than what weight?
choice_a: 10,000 pounds
choice_b: 5,000 pounds
choice_c: 16,000 pounds
choice_d: 26,001 pounds
explanation: The manual states Class A combination vehicles have a GCWR of 26,001 or more pounds, provided the GVWR of the vehicle(s) being towed is more than 10,000 pounds.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 6

question: Any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 or more pounds, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle not in excess of 10,000 pounds GVWR, falls into which class?
choice_a: Class C
choice_b: Class A
choice_c: Class B
choice_d: No CDL is required for this vehicle
explanation: The manual describes Class B (Heavy Straight Vehicles) as any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 or more pounds, or such a vehicle towing another vehicle not exceeding 10,000 pounds GVWR, including straight trucks and large buses.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 6

question: A single vehicle with a GVWR under 26,001 pounds falls into Class C and requires a CDL only under which condition?
choice_a: It is designed to carry 16 or more passengers including the driver, or is used to transport hazardous materials requiring placarding
choice_b: It is longer than 20 feet
choice_c: It has more than two axles
choice_d: It is registered under the International Registration Plan (IRP)
explanation: The manual states Class C vehicles fall under the CDL program only if designed to carry 16 or more passengers including the driver, or used to transport hazardous materials in quantities requiring placarding under 49 CFR Part 172, Subpart F.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 6-7

question: Drivers who wish to drive a vehicle with a design capacity to carry 16 or more people, including the driver, must add which endorsement?
choice_a: Passenger (P)
choice_b: School Bus (S)
choice_c: Tank Vehicle (N)
choice_d: Hazardous Materials (H)
explanation: The manual states drivers wishing to carry 16 or more people, including the driver, must add a passenger (P) endorsement, pass a special knowledge examination, and pass a Skills Test in a passenger vehicle; the endorsement applies in any class (A, B, or C).
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 7

question: A driver hauling material required to be placarded under 49 CFR Part 172, Subpart F must add a Hazardous Materials (H) endorsement, which also requires what additional step?
choice_a: A TSA background check including a review of criminal, immigration, and FBI records
choice_b: A state vision waiver
choice_c: An IFTA quarterly filing
choice_d: Fourteen days of supervised driving in a placarded vehicle
explanation: The manual explains that the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) and USDOT require background checks, including review of criminal, immigration, and FBI records, for drivers certified to transport hazardous materials.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 7

question: The Tank Vehicle (N) endorsement is required for a tank with an individual rated capacity of more than how many gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of at least how many gallons?
choice_a: More than 119 gallons individual; 1,000 gallons or more aggregate
choice_b: More than 500 gallons individual; 2,000 gallons or more aggregate
choice_c: More than 50 gallons individual; 500 gallons or more aggregate
choice_d: More than 200 gallons individual; 1,500 gallons or more aggregate
explanation: The manual defines a tank vehicle requiring the N endorsement as one with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate rated capacity of 1,000 gallons or more, permanently or temporarily attached to the vehicle or chassis.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 7

question: Why does the manual say a special knowledge examination is required before a Class A driver may add the Doubles/Triples (T) endorsement?
choice_a: Research shows considerable additional knowledge and skill is needed to safely pull double or triple trailers in various traffic conditions
choice_b: Federal law requires a TSA background check for all combination vehicles
choice_c: It is only available to drivers who already hold a Passenger endorsement
choice_d: Double and triple trailers cannot legally use air brakes
explanation: The manual states research shows considerable additional knowledge and skill is necessary to safely pull double and triple trailers, so a special knowledge examination on the problems posed by pulling multiple trailers must be passed to add the T endorsement.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 7

question: A driver who wants to drive a school bus in any class (A, B, or C) must add which endorsement, which requires both a special knowledge exam and a Skills Test in a school bus?
choice_a: School Bus (S)
choice_b: Passenger (P)
choice_c: Tank Vehicle (N)
choice_d: Restriction K
explanation: The manual states drivers who wish to drive a school bus must add a School Bus (S) endorsement to their CDL/CLP, pass a special knowledge examination on transporting passengers in a school bus, and pass Skills Tests in a school bus.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 7

question: Drivers of tank vehicles who haul hazardous materials or waste in amounts requiring placards must add which endorsement, showing they passed exams for both tank vehicles and hazardous materials?
choice_a: Combination Hazardous Materials and Tank Vehicle (X)
choice_b: Tank Vehicle (N)
choice_c: Hazardous Materials (H)
choice_d: Doubles/Triples (T)
explanation: The manual states drivers of tank vehicles hauling hazardous materials or waste requiring placards must add an X endorsement, showing they passed the special knowledge examinations for both tank vehicles and hazardous materials.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 7

question: Which endorsements, according to the manual, are the only ones that may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)?
choice_a: Passenger (P), School Bus (S), and Tank Vehicle (N)
choice_b: Hazardous Materials (H), Tank Vehicle (N), and Doubles/Triples (T)
choice_c: All six endorsements may be added to a CLP
choice_d: Passenger (P) and Hazardous Materials (H) only
explanation: The manual specifically notes that the only endorsements that may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit are Passenger (P), School Bus (S), and Tank Vehicle (N).
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 7

question: What does the federal 'K' restriction generally indicate on a CDL or CLP?
choice_a: The driver is restricted from operating a CMV in interstate commerce (intrastate only)
choice_b: The driver cannot operate a vehicle with a manual transmission
choice_c: The driver cannot operate a vehicle equipped with air brakes
choice_d: The driver is restricted from carrying passengers in a CMV bus
explanation: The manual explains that if an applicant certifies status as Non-Excepted or Excepted Intrastate, the state indicates on the CDL that the person is restricted from operating a CMV in interstate commerce, using the K restriction.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 8

question: Under restriction code L, what happens if an applicant does not take or fails the air brake component of the Knowledge Test, or performs the Skills Test in a vehicle without air brakes?
choice_a: The person is restricted from operating a CMV equipped with any type of air brakes
choice_b: The person must retake the entire General Knowledge Test
choice_c: The person is restricted only from operating tank vehicles
choice_d: The person automatically receives a K restriction instead
explanation: The manual states that under the L restriction, the state must indicate the person is restricted from operating a CMV equipped with any type of air brakes, including systems operating fully or partially on the air brake principle.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 8

question: A Colorado applicant must be at least 18 years of age to apply for a CDL Instruction Permit or receive a CDL. What additional restriction applies specifically to drivers 18 through 20 years of age in Colorado?
choice_a: They are issued the 'K' restriction, limiting them to operating a CDL vehicle only within the boundaries of Colorado
choice_b: They must renew their CDL every six months instead of every four years
choice_c: They may only hold a Class C CDL until age 21
choice_d: They are barred from adding any endorsements until age 21
explanation: The manual states you must be at least 18 to apply for a CDL Instruction Permit or CDL, and that drivers 18 through 20 years of age will be issued the 'K' restriction to operate a CDL vehicle only within the boundaries of Colorado.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 8

question: Which of the following is listed among the requirements to receive a Colorado CDL Instruction Permit?
choice_a: Clear Commercial Driver License Information System (CDLIS) and National Driver Register (NDR) record checks
choice_b: Complete 14 calendar days of behind-the-wheel training
choice_c: Hold a valid passport
choice_d: Provide two years of pay stubs from a trucking employer
explanation: The manual lists requirements to receive the CDL Instruction Permit including having a Colorado regular driver license, showing legal presence and identification, being at least 18, proof of SSN, current DOT medical certification, clearing CDLIS and NDR checks, passing the required CDL Knowledge Tests, and paying the fee.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 8

question: A Colorado CDL Instruction Permit allows the holder to operate the class of vehicle shown on the permit only under what condition?
choice_a: When accompanied by a person at least 21 years old who holds a valid CDL of the same class or higher, with required endorsements, seated closest to the driver
choice_b: Only during daylight hours
choice_c: Only within a 25-mile radius of the permit holder's residence
choice_d: Only after completing the On-Road Skills Test segment
explanation: The manual states the CDL Instruction Permit allows the holder to operate the vehicle class shown only when accompanied by a person at least 21 years of age who holds a valid CDL of the same class or higher, with the required endorsements, seated closest to the driver.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 8

question: The Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT) Final Rule went into compliance on what date, requiring applicants to demonstrate proficiency in knowledge and behind-the-wheel training through an FMCSA-standard program before earning a CDL?
choice_a: February 7, 2022
choice_b: January 30, 2014
choice_d: October 1, 2020
explanation: The manual states the entry-level driver training Final Rule went into compliance on February 7, 2022, establishing standards for knowledge and behind-the-wheel training that applicants must complete through a program meeting FMCSA standards.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 8

question: The CDL Skills Test consists of three segments that must be taken in a specific order, passing each before moving to the next. What is that order?
choice_a: Vehicle Inspection, Basic Vehicle Control, On-road driving
choice_b: On-road driving, Vehicle Inspection, Basic Vehicle Control
choice_c: Basic Vehicle Control, On-road driving, Vehicle Inspection
choice_d: Vehicle Inspection, On-road driving, Basic Vehicle Control
explanation: The manual states the CDL Skills Test consists of Vehicle Inspection, Basic Vehicle Control, and On-road driving, and that applicants must take the segments in that order, passing each one before moving to the next.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 10

question: According to the manual, when is a CMV driver considered to be operating in interstate commerce?
choice_a: When driving from one state to another, or when a trip within a state crosses into another state, or when cargo/passengers are part of a trip beginning or ending in another state
choice_b: Only when the vehicle physically crosses a state line on every single trip
choice_c: Whenever the driver holds a CDL issued by a state other than where they reside
choice_d: Only when hauling hazardous materials across state lines
explanation: The manual defines interstate commerce as driving from one state to another or a foreign country, driving between two places within a state where part of the trip crosses into another state, or where the cargo or passengers are part of a trip that began or will end in another state.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 11

question: For a first offense such as driving a CMV with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of .04% or higher, refusing alcohol testing, or leaving the scene of an accident involving a CMV, for how long will a driver lose their CDL, at a minimum?
choice_a: At least one year
choice_b: At least 30 days
choice_c: At least six months
choice_d: At least five years
explanation: The manual lists first-offense violations including BAC of .04% or higher, DUI, refusing testing, leaving the scene of an accident, and committing a felony involving a CMV as resulting in loss of CDL for at least one year.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 12

question: An applicant will be denied, or a driver will lose, their Hazardous Materials endorsement for which of the following reasons listed in the manual?
choice_a: Being wanted or under indictment for certain felonies
choice_b: Holding a Class C CDL instead of Class A
choice_c: Missing a single vehicle registration renewal deadline
choice_d: Operating exclusively in excepted interstate commerce
explanation: The manual lists being wanted or under indictment for certain felonies, along with factors such as not being a lawful permanent resident, renouncing U.S. citizenship, certain convictions, adjudicated lack of mental capacity, or being deemed a TSA security threat, as reasons a Hazardous Materials endorsement will be denied or lost; TSA background checks including fingerprinting are required to obtain the endorsement.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 13

question: According to the manual's rules on distracted driving, what is a CDL holder prohibited from doing while operating a CMV?
choice_a: Holding a mobile telephone to conduct a voice communication or dialing it by pressing more than a single button, and sending or reading text messages
choice_b: Using a factory-installed CB radio
choice_c: Speaking with a passenger seated in the vehicle
choice_d: Listening to the vehicle radio
explanation: The manual states drivers are not allowed to hold a mobile telephone to conduct a voice communication or dial it by pressing more than a single button, and are not allowed to send or read text messages while driving a CMV.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 1 - Introduction, p. 14

question: In which language(s) can a Colorado applicant take the CDL Knowledge Test, and in which language must the Hazmat Knowledge Test be taken?
choice_a: The CDL Knowledge Test is offered in English and Spanish; the Hazmat Knowledge Test is offered only in English
choice_b: Both the CDL and Hazmat Knowledge Tests are offered only in English
choice_c: The CDL Knowledge Test is offered only in English; the Hazmat Knowledge Test is offered in English and Spanish
choice_d: Both tests are offered in English, Spanish, and French
explanation: Per the Colorado DMV, the CDL Knowledge Test is available in English and Spanish, but the Hazmat Knowledge Test is only available in English.
source_note: Colorado DMV, First-Time CDL Driver (dmv.colorado.gov/first-time-cdl-driver)

question: In Colorado, how long must an applicant hold a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) before they are eligible to take the CDL Skills Test at an approved third-party testing facility?
choice_a: 14 calendar days
choice_b: 48 hours
choice_c: 30 calendar days
choice_d: There is no minimum holding period
explanation: Per the Colorado DMV, a CLP must be held for 14 calendar days before the CDL Skills Test can be taken, at an approved third-party testing facility.
source_note: Colorado DMV, First-Time CDL Driver (dmv.colorado.gov/first-time-cdl-driver)

question: How long is a Colorado Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) valid, and can it be renewed?
choice_a: It is valid for one year and is not eligible for renewal; all required exams must be retaken if a different class or endorsement is needed
choice_b: It is valid for six months and can be renewed once
choice_c: It is valid for two years and can be renewed indefinitely
choice_d: It is valid for 90 days and automatically converts to a CDL
explanation: Per the Colorado DMV, CLPs are valid for one year and are not eligible for renewal; if a different class or endorsement is needed, all required exams must be retaken.
source_note: Colorado DMV, First-Time CDL Driver (dmv.colorado.gov/first-time-cdl-driver)

question: In Colorado, how long are the results of a passed written CDL Knowledge Test valid for?
choice_a: Only for one issuance of a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)
choice_b: For the applicant's entire driving career
choice_c: For exactly five years, regardless of CLP status
choice_d: Indefinitely, as long as the applicant remains a Colorado resident
explanation: Per the Colorado DMV, the results of the written CDL Knowledge Test(s) are only valid for one issuance of a CLP.
source_note: Colorado DMV, First-Time CDL Driver (dmv.colorado.gov/first-time-cdl-driver)

question: How long is a standard Commercial Driver License (CDL) valid for in Colorado from the date of issuance?
choice_a: 4 years
choice_b: 2 years
choice_c: 6 years
choice_d: 8 years
explanation: Per the Colorado DMV, CDLs are valid for 4 years from the date of issuance in Colorado.
source_note: Colorado DMV, First-Time CDL Driver (dmv.colorado.gov/first-time-cdl-driver)

question: What does Colorado's Vets-2-Trucks program do for eligible servicemembers and recent veterans (within one year of discharge) seeking a CDL?
choice_a: It waives the driving Skills Test requirement, but the applicant must still pass the written knowledge exams
choice_b: It waives both the written knowledge exams and the Skills Test entirely
choice_c: It provides a state-funded truck for the first year of employment
choice_d: It automatically issues a CDL with all six endorsements
explanation: Per the Colorado DMV, the Vets-2-Trucks program helps Colorado servicemembers and recent veterans (within one year of discharge) qualify for a CDL by waiving the driving Skills Test requirement, though passing the written knowledge exams is still required.
source_note: Colorado DMV, First-Time CDL Driver (dmv.colorado.gov/first-time-cdl-driver)

question: Which state agency administers Colorado's CDL program, and where is its CDL Unit office located?
choice_a: The Colorado Department of Revenue, Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV), with its CDL Unit office at 3265 S Wadsworth Blvd, Lakewood
choice_b: The Colorado State Patrol, headquartered in Denver
choice_c: The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration regional office in Golden
choice_d: The Colorado Department of Transportation, Division of Highway Safety
explanation: Per the Colorado DMV, the CDL program is administered by the Colorado Department of Revenue, Division of Motor Vehicles, whose CDL Unit office is located at 3265 S Wadsworth Blvd, Lakewood, CO.
source_note: Colorado DMV, First-Time CDL Driver (dmv.colorado.gov/first-time-cdl-driver)

question: Under 49 CFR 383.135(a), what is the federal minimum passing standard used across all states, including Colorado, for CDL knowledge and skills tests?
explanation: 49 CFR 383.135(a) establishes an 80% minimum passing standard for CDL testing that is used across all states, including Colorado; official Colorado sources do not disclose a specific item count for the General Knowledge Test.
source_note: Colorado DMV, First-Time CDL Driver (dmv.colorado.gov/first-time-cdl-driver); 49 CFR 383.135(a)
